verdicts.title: More Cases Where the Kruskal-Katona Bound is Tight
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In graph theory, knowing the number of complete subgraphs with r vertices that a graph g has, limits the number of its complete subgraphs with s vertices, for s > r. A useful upper bound is provided by the Kruskal-Katona theorem, but this bound is often not tight. In this note, we add to the known cases where this bound is tight and begin an investigation of tight bounded graph sequences.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns tightness cases of the Kruskal-Katona bound for counting complete subgraphs in graphs, with no mention of EKR families, intersecting families, communication complexity, or discrepancy. It shares the Kruskal-Katona vocabulary but does not address the conjectured inequality linking shadow defect to spectral discrepancy.

verdicts.title: Tight bounds for Katona's shadow intersection theorem
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
A fundamental result in extremal set theory is Katona's shadow intersection theorem, which extends the Kruskal-Katona theorem by giving a lower bound on the size of the shadow of an intersecting family of $k$-sets in terms of its size. We improve this classical result and a related result of Ahlswede, Aydinian, and Khachatrian by proving tight bounds for families that can be quite small. For example, when $k=3$ our result is sharp for all families with $n$ points and at least $3n-7$ triples.
